pages.h1: Best AI coding tools for $20 a month or less
pages.title: Best AI Coding Tools for $20/Month or Less (2026)
pages.desc: AI coding tools with a paid plan at $20/month or less, ranked with vendor-verified prices checked 16 Oct 2026: Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot and more.
pages.summary: If you want the most capable tool for $20 a month or less, start with Cursor. Its Plus plan is $8/month, but it only includes Grok models. Claude Code comes with Claude Pro, at $17/month billed annually or $20 billed monthly. GitHub Copilot Pro ($10/month) is the pick if you want to stay in your current IDE. Zed Pro and JetBrains AI Pro are also $10/month. Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf), Devin, Kiro, Amp and Replit Core all list a $20 plan. Every price below is from the vendor's own pricing page, checked 16 Oct 2026.
pages.pick: Pick Cursor Plus if price matters most and Grok models are fine for you. Pick Claude Code through Claude Pro if you work in the terminal and want Anthropic's agent. Pick GitHub Copilot Pro, JetBrains AI Pro or Zed Pro ($10 each) if you want to keep your editor: Copilot covers most IDEs, JetBrains AI covers JetBrains IDEs, and Zed is its own fast editor. Pick Devin Desktop, Devin, Kiro or Amp at $20 if you want agent-first workflows, and Replit Core if you want to build and host in the browser with no local setup. Watch for usage limits. Several of these plans bill anything over the included usage at API prices.
faq: What is the cheapest paid AI coding plan on this list?
Cursor Plus at $8/month, as listed on cursor.com/pricing on 16 Oct 2026. It only includes Grok models, and third-party models need Premium ($30/month).
Is Claude Code under $20 a month?
Claude Code is included in Claude Pro, which is $17/month billed annually or $20 billed monthly (claude.com/pricing, checked 16 Oct 2026). There is no standalone free tier.
Do $20 plans include unlimited usage?

Not on the plans we checked. Devin Desktop and Devin Pro use quotas, with extra usage billed at API prices. Kiro meters usage in credits. Zed Pro includes $5 of tokens. Read each vendor's limits before you pay.

pages.desc: The best AI coding plans priced under $50/month, ranked with vendor pricing checked 16 Oct 2026: Cursor Premium, Copilot Pro+, Kiro Pro+, Bolt Pro and more.
pages.summary: Under $50 a month, Cursor Premium ($30/month) is our top pick. It gets 4x Plus usage, cloud agents, Bugbot reviews and third-party models, though those models are billed at API list price. Claude Code through Claude Pro ($20 monthly) is the terminal pick. Claude Max starts at $100, which is over this cap. GitHub Copilot Pro+ is $39/month, Kiro Pro+ $40/user/month, JetBrains AI Ultimate $30/month and Bolt Pro $25/month. pages.pick: Pick Cursor Premium if you want one AI-native editor with cloud agents and code review and you're happy to pay API prices for third-party models. Pick Copilot Pro+ for higher limits without leaving VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio, Eclipse or Xcode. Pick JetBrains AI Ultimate if you live in JetBrains IDEs. Pick Kiro Pro+ for spec-driven work on AWS. Pick Bolt Pro to build full-stack apps in the browser with no daily token cap. If $20 is your limit, see the $20 list.
faq: Which plans here are between $20 and $50 a month?
Bolt Pro ($25), Cursor Premium ($30), JetBrains AI Ultimate ($30), GitHub Copilot Pro+ ($39) and Kiro Pro+ ($40/user), all as listed on vendor pricing pages on 16 Oct 2026.
Is Claude Max under $50?
No. Claude Max starts at $100/month (claude.com/pricing, checked 16 Oct 2026). Under $50, Claude Code comes through Claude Pro.
Are there extra costs on top of these prices?

Often, yes. Cursor bills third-party models at API list price. Zed bills hosted usage beyond the included credit at API price plus 10%. Kiro sells add-on credits at $0.04 each. Prices also exclude tax.

pages.h1: Best free AI coding tools (no subscription)
pages.title: Best Free AI Coding Tools (No Subscription, 2026)
pages.desc: AI coding tools you can use with no subscription: Cline, Zed, Amp, OpenHands and Aider, with what you still pay for, checked on vendor pages 16 Oct 2026.
pages.summary: For AI coding with no subscription, Cline is our top pick. It's an open-source agent for VS Code and the CLI, and you pay only for model usage, with your own keys or at cost. Zed is free forever with your own API keys or external agents. Amp's Hobby plan is free with all features and bring-your-own keys. OpenHands is free to run locally, and its cloud tier allows 10 conversations a day. Aider is free, open-source terminal software. The catch: unless you run a local model, you still pay a model provider. If you want usage included at $0, see the free-tier list.
pages.pick: Pick Cline if you want an agent inside VS Code and full control of spend. Pick Zed if you want a fast free editor and already have API keys or an external agent. Pick Amp if you want to reuse your ChatGPT or Claude subscriptions in an agent. Pick OpenHands if you want an autonomous agent you can self-host and audit. Pick Aider if you live in the terminal and want clean git commits. Continue is listed last for transparency: it's frozen after Cursor acquired it, so only use it if you accept no updates.
faq: Are these AI coding tools really free?
The software is free, but most of them call a paid model API with your key or the vendor's provider at cost. Cline, Aider and OpenHands say this on their own pages. A local model avoids API bills.
Which free tool works inside VS Code?
Cline runs in VS Code and the CLI. Its JetBrains extension is listed under Enterprise (cline.bot/pricing, checked 16 Oct 2026). Continue also ran in VS Code but is no longer maintained.
What's the difference between this list and the free-tier list?

This list covers tools with no subscription, where you bring your own model. The free-tier list covers paid products whose free plan includes some hosted usage, such as GitHub Copilot Free or Cursor Free.

Claude Code (Anthropic's terminal agent, via a paid Claude plan) and Aider (free, open source, commits to git). Cline also has a CLI.

pages.title: Best AI Coding Agents in 2026: Ranked and Compared
pages.desc: The best AI coding agents in 2026, from Claude Code and Devin to Cline, OpenHands, Amp and Kiro, with verified pricing and limits checked 16 Oct 2026.
pages.summary: For an agent that works across your repo, Claude Code is our top pick: Anthropic's terminal agent, included with Claude Pro ($17/month annually). Cursor pairs its editor with agents and cloud automations. Devin takes whole tickets in the cloud and opens pull requests, but cloud agents need Pro ($20/month). Cline and OpenHands are open-source agents where you pay only for inference. Amp lets you reuse existing model subscriptions. Kiro is AWS's spec-driven agent with a perpetual free tier. Checked 16 Oct 2026.
pages.pick: Pick Claude Code if you want the agent in your terminal and repo. Pick Cursor if you want agents inside an editor, plus cloud agents on Premium. Pick Copilot if agents should live in GitHub and your IDE. Its free plan has no cloud agent. Pick Devin to delegate scoped tickets and review the PRs. Pick Cline or OpenHands for open-source agents you control, with OpenHands also self-hostable. Pick Kiro for spec-first work on AWS and Amp to reuse ChatGPT or Claude subscriptions.
faq: Which AI coding agents are open source?
Cline (Apache-2.0) and OpenHands (MIT), per their GitHub and pricing pages checked 16 Oct 2026. Both are free to run, and you pay for model inference.
Can I try a coding agent for free?

Yes. Kiro has a perpetual free tier with 50 credits. Devin's Free plan has a light quota but no cloud agents. OpenHands Cloud Individual allows 10 conversations a day. Amp Hobby is free with your own keys. Claude Code has no standalone free tier.
Do I still need to review agent output?
Yes. Devin's own model is that the agent opens pull requests for you to review, and every tool here can make mistakes. Treat agent changes like a colleague's PR.

faq: Which AI pair programmer works in the most editors?
GitHub Copilot. GitHub lists VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Eclipse, Xcode, the CLI, GitHub.com and GitHub Mobile (checked 16 Oct 2026).
Is there a free AI pair programmer?
Copilot Free and Cursor Free include limited usage. Zed Personal and Aider are free software where you use your own model keys.
Pair programmer or coding agent: what's the difference?
A pair programmer suggests and edits as you work. An agent takes a task and carries it out across files, often in the cloud. See our coding agents list for agent-first tools.

pages.desc: AI coding tools for beginners and non-developers: Lovable, Bolt.new, Replit, GitHub Copilot and Cursor, with free plans and prices verified 16 Oct 2026.
pages.summary: If you're new to code and want to build something, start with Lovable or Bolt.new. Both turn plain-language prompts into web apps in the browser and have free plans. Lovable gives 5 build credits a day, up to 30 a month. Bolt gives 300K tokens a day and 1M a month. Replit builds, hosts and deploys from one browser workspace, with Core at $20/month. If you want to learn to code in a real editor, GitHub Copilot Free and Cursor Free cost nothing to start. Checked 16 Oct 2026.
pages.pick: Pick Lovable if you're a non-developer who wants a working web app from a description. Pick Bolt.new for the same thing with a token-based free tier. Pick Replit if you want building, a database and hosting in one place with nothing to install. Pick Copilot or Cursor once you want to write and understand the code yourself in an editor.
faq: Can I build an app with AI without knowing how to code?
Lovable and Bolt.new are built for that: both create web apps from chat prompts in the browser. You'll still need to test what they build, and larger projects use up credits or tokens.
What's free for beginners?

Lovable Free (5 build credits a day, up to 30 a month), Bolt Free (300K tokens a day, 1M a month), Copilot Free and Cursor Free, all per vendor pages checked 16 Oct 2026. We couldn't confirm Replit's free plan limits.
Should a beginner use an AI code editor?
If you want to learn programming, yes. Copilot or Cursor in an editor shows you real code. If you only want a finished app, a browser builder like Lovable or Bolt is simpler.

Can these tools deploy my app?
